queries: symbol grounding problem remains open large language models 2025 survey

sources_considered.why: January 2025 survey that lists symbol grounding among problems LLMs still need to solve.
June 2025 benchmark paper. It says there are no shared criteria for when a solution is achieved, and it notes Steels's partial-solution view.
Philosophy paper on vector grounding, revised later. Not needed.
October 2025, after the post, and only a secondary summary.

receipt.public_excerpt: A number of foundational problems -- embodiment, symbol grounding, causality and memory -- are required to be addressed for LLMs to attain human-level general intelligence.

evidence_items.explanation: This 2025 survey treats symbol grounding as a foundational problem LLMs still need to address. That fits 'not systematically solved'.

receipt.public_excerpt: Moreover, the absence of shared scoring criteria has made it difficult to determine when and how a solution to either problem might be said to have been achieved.

evidence_items.explanation: A June 2025 paper says the field had no shared criteria for even calling symbol grounding solved. That supports the claim that no systematic solution was accepted.

receipt.public_excerpt: Steels argued that the symbol grounding problem itself has been “solved” to some extent, but presented a new challenge of constructing autonomous meaning networks [13].

evidence_items.explanation: A minority view holds that grounding is partly solved. Even this view is qualified ('to some extent') and names a remaining challenge, so it does not show a systematic solution.

unresolved_gaps: No single authoritative consensus statement exists. The finding rests on how 2025 papers describe the problem.
